what_happened: While job 20261030-214204-x2fz was running, its producer finished and left 9.4 GB of free disk. The pre-check guard needs 10 GB. If nothing had been done, the job would have ended failed on low disk before its checks ran, as job d103 did earlier. The the person running Athena freed about 1 GB by hand (uv and npm caches and the workspace target directory), which put free space over the guard. No criterion or check had failed. This was an the person running Athena intervention to avoid a failure.
cause: Athena owns no disk lifecycle. Caches (uv, npm, build targets) and finished workspaces are never cleaned. The 10 GB guard only reports failure and does not make room, and nothing reclaims regenerable space between the producer stage and the checks. The fix that would hold or clean on low disk (b5hm) is queued but not landed, so each job near the threshold depends on an the person running Athena noticing and clearing space in time.
prevention: When free space falls below the guard before the checks, Athena should reclaim regenerable space itself (uv and npm caches, build targets of finished or idle workspaces) and re-measure. If that is not enough, it should put the job on hold, not mark it failed, and resume when space is available. This is the b5hm fix: bring it forward and have it include the automatic cleanup step as well as the hold. Add a test that simulates 9.4 GB free after the producer and expects cleanup and then a pass, or a hold with no failed state.
proposed_request: When the free-disk guard finds less free space than its threshold before a job's checks or verification, Athena must not end the job failed. First it deletes regenerable space it owns: uv and npm caches and the build target directories of finished or idle job workspaces. It then re-measures free space. If space is now at or above the threshold, the job continues. If not, the job is put on hold with a clear message stating free space and threshold, and it resumes on its own, or by `athena retry`, once space is available, without repeating the producer's spend. Acceptance: a test with 9.4 GB free against a 10 GB guard shows cleanup runs and the job continues; a test where cleanup frees too little shows the job held and not failed, and a later retry runs the checks without re-running the producer; cleanup never deletes the current job's committed work or any records; the change is recorded in the changelog.
